purpose: Independent, per-invariant classification of all 37 invariants in docs/HEADROOM-ARCHITECTURE-INVARIANTS.md. Classification requires either a currently-passing test directly exercising the invariant, or code personally traced by this auditor this session -- documentation prose alone is never sufficient for PROVEN_*.
environmentNote: This worktree was initially checked out at a divergent later commit (81fd6c4) that predated Phase 3F.1.5.R entirely (invariant #37, the safe-failure architecture, and docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation-closure.md were all absent). Corrected via `git reset --hard ea82ee80f4528117e7dc6669be8e1ebf28b24108` (the specified starting commit, clean working tree, no uncommitted work lost) before this audit began.

invariants.title: Source evidence controls contractual truth
invariants.evidence: IRRule.provenance.sourceCitation and MaterialSemanticUnit.anchors[].sourceCitation are required, non-optional fields throughout lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts and semantic-coverage/types.ts. tests/foundation-audit/provenance-chain-backward-trace.test.ts directly traces a compiled conclusion back to its real source citation. Personally re-verified this session via reconciliation.ts's findAnchoredRule, which refuses to credit a rule with no matching sourceCitation.

invariants.title: Source evidence controls financial truth
invariants.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma's ExternalInputRecord model (sourceRef/reviewStatus/asOfDate/fieldKey, linked to FinancialState/Facility) provides real structural support for exactly this guarantee, confirmed by direct schema read this session.
invariants.gap: I did not personally re-trace every financial-fact write path (connectors, manual entry, promotion) this session to confirm ExternalInputRecord population is actually enforced (not merely available) on every code path that writes a FinancialState/Facility fact. Marked PARTIALLY_PROVEN rather than PROVEN because the structural capability existing is not the same as every write path being audited to actually use it.

invariants.title: Every material contractual conclusion preserves provenance
invariants.evidence: Same evidentiary basis as #1 -- provenance is a required, non-optional field on IRRule/IRDefinition/MaterialSemanticUnit, and tests/foundation-audit/provenance-chain-backward-trace.test.ts exercises the full chain.

invariants.title: Every material financial value preserves provenance
invariants.evidence: Same basis as #2.

invariants.title: AI may interpret semantic variability
invariants.evidence: The semantic compiler (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/compile.ts) is the only layer that calls an LLM for interpretation; deterministic layers (structural parsing, reconciliation, operative-state) never do. Confirmed by reading semantic-coverage/types.ts's own Independence Contract, which forbids Layer A/B/C from importing the compiler.

invariants.title: Deterministic software owns arithmetic and trusted state
invariants.evidence: lib/covenant-engine.ts, lib/solver/*, lib/financial-core/* perform all arithmetic in plain TypeScript/Decimal; verified this session that computeOperativeContractState, reconcileFrozenInventory, and the safe-failure service.ts are all pure/deterministic functions with zero LLM calls.

invariants.title: Do not enumerate every covenant formulation
invariants.evidence: Not independently re-verified this session -- this is a design-history claim (FormulaType vs CalculationRuleKind) rather than something with a single test to point at. No counterexample found, but I did not audit the full IR schema for enum sprawl this session.

invariants.title: New drafting should ordinarily require new semantic interpretation, not new application code
invariants.evidence: Same basis as #7 -- a design-philosophy invariant not independently re-audited this session.

invariants.title: Unsupported semantics must be surfaced, not coerced
invariants.evidence: reconciliation.ts's UNSUPPORTED/UNREPRESENTED coverage states, and this session's own tests/foundation-audit/cross-module-propagation-chains.test.ts Chain 1 and adversarial-foundation-matrix.test.ts Case 7 (an unsupported expression correctly reaches UNREPRESENTED and produces a persisted ClaimReviewItem, never silently coerced into a false success state).

invariants.title: Missing context must be surfaced, never silently treated as nothing more to find
invariants.evidence: SOURCE_CONTEXT_INCOMPLETE coverage state exists and is exercised by tests/contract-model/semantic-coverage-fault-injection.test.ts; DangerousUnaccountedReason.NO_CANDIDATE_EVER_DISCOVERED is a first-class, never-silent classification confirmed by reading reconciliation.ts directly this session.

invariants.title: Ambiguous document relationships remain unresolved until real evidence resolves them
invariants.evidence: resolveUniqueNodeByRef/resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef's UNIQUE/AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND three-way axis, personally traced in lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts this session, and exercised by tests/foundation-audit/combined-failures.test.ts's duplicate-label case and this session's own Chain 2/4 and adversarial Case 2.

invariants.title: Amendments preserve history and effective dating
invariants.evidence: buildProvisionChain/appliedChain filtering by asOfDate, personally traced in operative-state.ts; tests/contract-model/phase-2g-amendment-precedence.test.ts and phase-3f1-operative-state-honesty.test.ts (file names confirmed present, not opened line-by-line this session).

invariants.title: Superseded language must never silently appear current
invariants.evidence: The NodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus mechanism (fail-closed to UNKNOWN by default) is real and directly exercised by this session's own adversarial-foundation-matrix.test.ts Case 5 and Case 8, and by tests/contract-model/node-supersession-awareness.test.ts. auditOperativeStateForUnits's STALE_SUPERSEDED_TEXT_CREDITED path is proven for SECTION-kind provisions (Chain 1/4 in this session's cross-module-propagation-chains.test.ts).
invariants.gap: This session's own Chain 2 test (tests/foundation-audit/cross-module-propagation-chains.test.ts) proves a REAL counterexample for DEFINITION-kind provisions: an independently-confirmed AMBIGUOUS defined term can still reach FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED in semantic-coverage because auditOperativeStateForUnits never checks candidateSourceNodeIds and DEFINITION-kind provisions never populate sectionRef. This is a genuine, reproduced violation of invariant #13's letter for one specific code path (DEFINITION-kind operative-state ambiguity reaching semantic-coverage) -- not a wholesale failure of the invariant, since the SECTION-kind case and the direct operative-state layer itself both remain honest. Classified PARTIALLY_PROVEN rather than VIOLATED because the invariant holds everywhere else this session checked, and the one gap has a narrow, precisely-identified blast radius (see Section 27's Chain 2 report and Section 30 finding SP-1).

invariants.title: Semantic understanding and calculation capability are separate trust dimensions
invariants.evidence: IRRule.sufficiency (COMPLETE/PARTIAL/etc.) is tracked independently of whether a registered evaluator exists for the rule's shape (lib/solver/coverage.ts's classifyCompanyCoverage), confirmed by reading covenant-engine.ts's routing logic this session.

invariants.title: No rule is executable merely because its fields are present
invariants.evidence: tests/solver/coverage-gate.test.ts directly tests classifyCompanyCoverage/determineCoverage's exact-shape-match requirement (file confirmed present, assertNoDoubleCounting test read in full this session).

invariants.title: AI output is not trusted merely because it is schema-valid JSON
invariants.evidence: semantic/compile.ts and stage-verification.ts both run independent verification (semantic-verification/verify.ts) after schema-valid compilation, confirmed by reading pipeline call order this session; reconciliation.ts's own FULLY_REPRESENTED_REVIEW_REQUIRED vs FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED distinction (confirmed via this session's own Chain 3 test) directly proves schema-valid output alone is insufficient for VERIFIED status.

invariants.title: Independent verification remains architecturally distinct from compilation
invariants.evidence: tests/contract-model/semantic-verification-independence.test.ts (file confirmed present) plus this session's own read of semantic-verification/types.ts's Independence Contract header, structurally identical to semantic-coverage's own (personally read in full this session).

invariants.title: Coverage auditing remains meaningfully independent (shared-substrate failure mode)
invariants.evidence: semantic-coverage/types.ts's own header comment (read in full this session) explicitly discloses the shared-StructuralIndex risk and names Phase 2F's blind-run precedent verbatim, with raw-source-fallback.ts as the disclosed partial mitigation. This is a case where the invariant's OWN standard is 'disclose the risk, do not pretend it's eliminated' -- the disclosure itself, not a false claim of independence, is what proves compliance here.

invariants.title: Tenant isolation is mandatory
invariants.evidence: tests/foundation-audit/semantic-cache-cross-tenant.test.ts (read in full this session -- confirms compile.ts's cache key now includes companyId) and this session's own adversarial-foundation-matrix.test.ts Case 6 (a NEW, genuinely adversarial concurrent cross-tenant upload race, executed against real Postgres this session, confirming @@unique([companyId, contentHash]) prevents any cross-tenant dedup even under a real race).

invariants.title: Instrument isolation is mandatory
invariants.evidence: tests/foundation-audit/tenant-instrument-drafting-collision.test.ts (file confirmed present) plus this session's own adversarial-foundation-matrix.test.ts Case 4 (identical defined term, identical sectionRef label, two different documents -- confirmed no cross-document/instrument leakage in either definition resolution or persisted ClaimReviewItem identity, executed against real Postgres).

invariants.title: Every material state transition is reproducible and versioned
invariants.evidence: tests/foundation-audit/combined-failures.test.ts's own ingestion-order-invariance test (read in full this session): computeOperativeContractState produces byte-identical candidateTexts regardless of effect ingestion order. computeSemanticUnitId/computeCoverageEntryId are content-derived (personally read identity.ts this session), never array-position-derived.

invariants.title: Headroom State supports incremental recomputation
invariants.evidence: docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md names 'Living Headroom State' as Phase 6, a future phase this repository has not yet built (the roadmap's own 'Current phase' marker still reads Phase 2 complete / recommends Phase 3A, though the repo has visibly progressed to Phase 3F.1.5.R -- a stale marker, disclosed as an informational finding, not a numbered-invariant violation on its own).
invariants.blockerRiskAnalysis: NOT a trust-critical invariant per this audit's own list, and the absence of proof reflects the feature genuinely not existing yet, not a hidden defect in an existing system. Not dangerous: there is no Headroom State today whose incremental-recomputation correctness could be silently wrong.

invariants.title: Source / normalized / contractual / calculated financial values remain four distinct layers
invariants.evidence: FinancialState (source facts) vs. covenant-engine.ts's computed metrics vs. IR-derived contractual capacity are structurally distinct in the schema and code, confirmed by this session's own schema read.
invariants.gap: Did not independently re-verify every consumer never collapses these into one number this session -- relying on schema separation as strong but not exhaustive evidence.

invariants.evidence: ClaimReviewItem/OperativeProvisionView both carry explicit status/reviewRequired/unresolvedIssues fields designed for exactly this. This session did not audit any actual customer-facing app/ page's rendering of these fields end-to-end (confirmed the safe-failure architecture is not yet wired into any live app/ route at all -- see Section 27's disclosed gap), so the DATA exists but I did not verify the UI actually surfaces it.

invariants.evidence: Not independently re-audited this session across app/ pages.

invariants.evidence: No 'Ask Headroom' conversational surface was located or audited this session; likely not yet built given the roadmap's current phase.

invariants.evidence: Personally confirmed this session: app/[companyId]/simulate/SimulateClient.tsx line 238 calls the real, unmodified simulateDebtIncurrence -- the exact concrete precedent the invariant names, verified verbatim rather than trusted from documentation.

invariants.title: Regression packages are never relabeled unseen
invariants.evidence: This session's own Section 28 script (scripts/phase-3f1-6-known-package-regression.ts) explicitly disclosed CONMED/DSGR/FWRG/LSB as permanent regression evidence and never proposed treating any of them as unseen; docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation-closure.md and run-cross-dataset-v3.ts (read this session) both explicitly reaffirm this.

invariants.title: No benchmark-specific production logic
invariants.evidence: Section 30's exhaustive grep (this session) of lib/ and app/ for FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR/Coherent/Matthews found zero hardcoded branches in matching/decision logic. The two real hits in production code (lib/dashboard-service.ts's SOLVER_CONTEXT_ENTITY_DEFAULTS, lib/coherent.ts's PROTECTED_COMPANY_IDS) are a generalized lookup-table-with-sane-fallback and a delete-protection allowlist respectively -- neither alters covenant-answer correctness or matching/decision logic, and both are honestly disclosed in their own header comments. See 28-static-danger-pattern-audit.json finding SP-9 for full detail.

invariants.title: Reviewed human corrections should become reusable precedent where appropriate
invariants.evidence: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-precedent/* is a real, substantial module (precedent-integration.ts plus 7+ dedicated test files confirmed present this session, including semantic-precedent-corrections.test.ts and semantic-precedent-anti-memorization.test.ts) directly implementing this.

invariants.title: Local bugs do not redefine the strategic roadmap
invariants.evidence: Phase 3F.1.5.R's own closure doc (read this session) is itself a model instance: 4 residual defects diagnosed -> generalized remediation -> regression test -> continue roadmap, explicitly never proposing an architecture change.

invariants.title: Any strategic architecture change requires an explicit ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_PROPOSAL
invariants.evidence: No ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_PROPOSAL document exists anywhere in docs/ (confirmed by directory listing this session), consistent with no undisclosed strategic drift having occurred; the mechanism's format is fully specified in the invariants doc itself.

invariants.title: Never blend two evaluation paths for the same scope
invariants.evidence: tests/solver/coverage-gate.test.ts's assertNoDoubleCounting tests, read in full this session -- both the passing and throwing cases are directly exercised, and lib/covenant-engine.ts:1102 calls it as a real production gate.

invariants.title: A verification/sufficiency check that is too strict fails falsely safe, not safe
invariants.evidence: The invariant's own named precedent (Phase C's byte-exact citation bug) is historical; I did not independently re-test any current sufficiency check for over-strictness this session.

invariants.title: Competing event-sourcing or truth logs must be explicitly reconciled or linked, never left to silently diverge
invariants.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma's DebtEvent.sourceLedgerEntryId (the invariant's own named example field) is, confirmed by grep across the entire lib/ and app/ trees this session, NEVER WRITTEN anywhere in production code -- only read (lib/financial-core-db/adapter.ts:194, with a `?? undefined` fallback for the always-null case). This is exactly the pattern invariant #35 was written to forbid: 'a schema field exists for exactly this purpose while remaining permanently unpopulated in practice.'
invariants.severityNote: Trust-critical per this audit's list; VIOLATED on a trust-critical invariant is a certification BLOCKER per this audit's own charter. Scope is narrow (one specific link field, not a systemic reconciliation failure across many logs), but it is a real, reproducible violation, not a documentation gap.

invariants.title: A degraded/tolerant parsing boundary must degrade to an honest unknown value, never crash or silently drop the surrounding unit of work
invariants.evidence: This session's own review of ~20 catch blocks across lib/contract-model, lib/connectors, lib/onboarding (Section 30) found the overwhelming majority correctly degrade to an explicit FAILED/failed:true status with the error message preserved (stage-inventory.ts, stage-verification.ts, stage-rule-extraction.ts, ai-inventory.ts, semantic/caller.ts, semantic-verification/reviewer.ts all confirmed this pattern by direct reading). tests/contract-model/discovery-fail-closed.test.ts and pass-b-semantic role-enum-crash fix (named in the invariant itself) confirmed present.

invariants.title: NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE
invariants.evidence: The ClaimReviewItem/ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision architecture is real, schema-backed, and this session's own Section 28 regression (scripts/phase-3f1-6-known-package-regression.ts) proves ZERO silent material failures across FWRG (398/398), LSB (79/79), and DSGR (2299/2299) -- every CRITICAL/MATERIAL semantic unit in a non-VERIFIED coverage state produced exactly one persisted ClaimReviewItem, confirmed against real Postgres this session. This session's own Chain 1/3/4 tests (cross-module-propagation-chains.test.ts) prove the full chain composes for structural-health, verification-withholding, and SECTION-kind amendment-ambiguity uncertainty.
invariants.gap: Two disclosed, material gaps: (1) this session's own Chain 2 test proves a genuine counterexample -- DEFINITION-kind operative-state ambiguity can silently fail to reach semantic-coverage and can even resolve to a confident-but-wrong FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED, meaning the ONE thing invariant #37 exists to make structurally impossible (a claim disappearing with no trace) is reproducibly possible for this specific code path; (2) the entire safe-failure architecture, confirmed by grep this session, has exactly ONE wired emission point (the offline coverage-auditor script/test path) and is NOT called from any live app/ route or from the real document-onboarding pipeline (app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/actions.ts) -- so in the CURRENT live product, no document a real customer uploads today ever reaches this architecture at all; every guarantee above is proven only for the offline/script-invoked path.
invariants.severityNote: Trust-critical; the Chain 2 gap and the not-wired-to-live-routes gap are both reported as BLOCKER-class findings in Section 27's own verdict, not merely informational.

summary.note: Each of the 37 invariants above carries exactly one classification; counts sum to 37. VIOLATED (#35) and the two PARTIALLY_PROVEN trust-critical items with disclosed live gaps (#13, #37) are the three findings this audit treats as certification-relevant; #35 alone is a BLOCKER per this audit's own charter ('VIOLATED on a trust-critical invariant is itself a BLOCKER').
